dataset.name: Leaf mass per area and leaf water content measurements from field survey in association with NEON AOP survey, East River, CO 2018
description: Leaf area, wet, and dry weights for leaf samples from sites where field sampling was conducted during the 2018 National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) Airborne Observation Platform (AOP) imaging spectroscopy and lidar surveys in Gunnison County, Colorado. The sampling sites were located across East River, Washington Gulch, Slate River, and Coal Creek watersheds and contained a mixture of meadow, shrub, and tree sampling sites. This data package contains the leaf area and wet and dry weights for leaves from tree and shrub sampling sites, as well as samples for meadow species present within a given sampling area. Associated data packages contain species composition information at the plot level (DOI: 10.15485/1618130), as well as additional biogeochemical, microbial, and geophysical data as they become available. For full documentation, please see associated reference.

This package contains zipped folders of all scans that were used for area calculations for both sampling sites (tree/shrub, site_scans.zip) as well as representative samples from a daily sampling area of meadow species that were found in the 1 m plots (meadow_area_scans.zip). It also contains the macro code that was used in ImageJ for processing of the area calculations. Finally, it includes excel files with the area (cm2), wet weight (g), dry weight (g), leaf mass per area (LMA, g/m2), and leaf water content (%) for each set of scans.

measurementTechnique: For trees and shrubs, an LMA sample was collected for each individual sampled. These samples were collected from sun-lit leaves, with enough sample for 30-40 g of fresh leaf material (not including stem or woody material) plus enough additional leaves to mostly fill a 8.5 x 11 in scanner bed without overlap for LMA determination. We identified branches that were sunlit and cut 2-3 small branches by slingshot or pole clippers depending on canopy height. We assessed samples to avoid excessive herbivore damage, discoloration, or epiphylls. Samples for LMA determination were subset from the main sample and placed in a gallon polyethylene bag with a damp paper towel keeping foliage attached to the stem whenever possible to prevent water loss. As much air as possible was removed from the bag before sealing, while careful that leaves were not crushed or folded, and placed in a cooler with ice.

At the end of the day’s sampling, from the meadow fractional cover documentation, a team member collected a list of the species that were identified within the meadow plots during the day’s sampling. For each of these species, take samples from five different individuals across the sample area, and outside of the sampling plots, for LMA calculations. We collected entire stems where possible and placed them in a gallon polyethylene bag with a damp paper towel to prevent rapid dehydration of leaves. This method allowed for an average LMA to be calculated by species for the plot site, while having a feasible amount of scanning work to complete, and allowing transport back to the laboratory before excessive wilting affects the ability to retrieve accurate area measurements in the scanning process.

LMA was determined for each site based on if the site comprised an individual plant (tree or shrub), or was a meadow site that contained a mixture of individuals. For each individual tree and shrub site sampled, and each meadow species sampled across meadow sites for a sampling area, scans were completed on mature leaves that were transported on ice from the field. Leaves were selected to fill an 8.5 x 11 in scanner bed that did not have holes or significant herbivore damage, in order to fill the area without leaves touching or overlapping. The 300 dpi scans were completed and checked to ensure there was no overlap or extension of leaves outside of the scan area. The leaves included in the scans were then weighed, dried at 65 ℃, and reweighed to determine water content and dry mass. Leaf area was calculated for each 300 dpi scan with ImageJ automation using macros and batch processing. Contrast parameters were adjusted in the macros code to capture the entire leaf area for a variety of leaf sizes, ranging from pine needles to broad leaves. If automation does not capture the full leaf area, edits to the code provide a manual selection option before calculating leaf area. The dry mass was divided by the scan area to determine LMA in g m-2. The LMA values found for individual trees and shrubs were assumed to represent the average values within the crown.

Details of ImageJ processing (run on Mac OS):
1) Open the ImageJ_leaf_area_batch.txt file in ImageJ by going to "Plugins" --> "Macros" --> "Install". Then, hit 'b' on the keyboard to open the folder where scans are saved.
Note: The program will run through the calculation for the first scan in the file. It will pause after subtracting the background to provide an option for manual selection
2) If you want to do a manual selection, use the wand tool, and hold down shift as you select all leaf area that should be included in the calculation, then press ok.
3) If the automated calculation looks great press ok (without using the wand tool).
4) A window will pop up with the document (scan) name and leaf area calculation, along with a results table.
5) The program automatically moves onto the next scan where the process repeats until all calculations are done.
